paper_title: Langfristige Wohnstandortpräferenzen: Schlechte Nachrichten für ländliche Regionen
caption: Haushalte im oberen Quintil der westdeutschen Nettohaushaltseinkommen
model_annotation:
The graph compares the percentage distribution of households in the upper quintile of net household income in West Germany across different regions and housing types from 1984 to 2017. The x-axis is labeled with years, ranging from 1984 to 2015 in five-year intervals, and the y-axis represents the percentage, ranging from 0% to 35% in increments of 5%. The six lines on the graph represent different categories of regions and housing types. 
Line 1, represented by blue crosses, shows 'Städtische Regionen, Ein- und Zweifamilienhäuser' (urban regions, single and two-family houses) starting at around 29% in 1984, peaking at 32% in 1991, and ending at approximately 32% in 2017. Line 2, depicted by blue circles, represents 'Städtische Regionen, Mehrfamilienhäuser in Wohngebieten, überwiegend Neubauestand' (urban regions, multi-family houses in residential areas, predominantly new buildings) starting at around 15%, decreasing to 12% in 1995, and ending at 14% in 2017. Line 3, shown as blue triangles, indicates 'Städtische Regionen, Mehrfamilienhäuser in Wohngebieten, überwiegend Altbaubestand' (urban regions, multi-family houses in residential areas, predominantly old buildings) beginning at 12%, decreasing to 7% in 2004, and rising to 10% in 2017. Line 4, represented by solid blue squares, shows 'Städtische Regionen, Mehrfamilienhäuser in zentralen Lagen' (urban regions, multi-family houses in central locations) starting at 15%, reaching 18% in 2007, and ending at 16% in 2017. Line 5, depicted by a dotted green line, represents 'Ländliche Regionen, Ein- und Zweifamilienhäuser' (rural regions, single and two-family houses) starting at 22%, peaking at 25% in 1993, and ending at around 20% in 2017. Line 6, shown as a solid green line, indicates 'Ländliche Regionen, Mehrfamilienhäuser' (rural regions, multi-family houses) beginning at 16%, decreasing to 6% in 2009, and rising slightly to 8% in 2017.
